subject: Halt execution of function until all observers are validated

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Halt execution of function until all observers are validated
parts:
Hi

I'm developing a shiny app that lets the user upload a set of files and perform an analysis on each of them. The result of the analysis is then send back to the user with a custom shiny output. Because the size of the analysis result is rather big, I want to send it for each analysis separately, instead of pooling everything together.

I'm having trouble with getting this to work as I cannot find a way to halt my for loop until the result has been send. To illustrate my approach here is some pseudo code:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    dataAdded <- reactiveValues(counter=0)
    dataStore <- list()
    
    dataGenerator <- observe({
        if(input$analysisButton == 0) return(c())
        
        files <- isolate({input$datafiles})
        
        for(i in files) {
            result <- doExpensiveAnalysis(i)
            index <- length(dataStore)+1
            dataStore[[index]] <<- result
            dataAdded$counter <<- isolate(dataAdded$counter)+1
        }
    })
    data <- reactive({
        index <- dataAdded$counter
        if(index != 0) {
            do.call('renderData', dataStore[[length(dataStore)]])
        }
    })
    output$result <- reactive({data()})
}

While this might be the wrong approach, the main idea is this: On the server there is a variable (dataStore) holding on to the results in a list. An observer depends on a button and when executing, loops through the files, analyse them, adds them to the dataStore and notifies the server that the dataStore has been updated by elevating the reactive value dataAdded$counter by one. Another reactive expression depends on the dataAdded$counter and reads the last value of the dataStore, do some preprocessing and sets it to the client (via output$result).

The problem is that data() is not evaluated each time data$Added$counter is increased, but only once the for-loop in dataGenerator is completed. The result of this is that only the result of the last analysis is ever sent to the client.

Is there a way to force evaluation of a reactive expression within another function? or is there a better setup than this that achieves the same thing?

best

Thomas

messages.subject: Re: Halt execution of function until all observers are validated
parts: I got this solved by changing the code up and using invalidateLater. The new structure is roughly:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    dataAdded <- reactiveValues(counter=0)
    dataStore <- list()

dataFiles <- c()
    analysisButtonCount <- 0
    
    dataGenerator <- observe({
        if(input$analysisButton == 0) return(c())
        
        if(input$analysisButton != analysisButtonCount) {
            dataFiles <<- isolate({input$datafiles})
            analysisButtonCount <<- input$analysisButton
        }
        
        result <- doExpensiveAnalysis(dataFiles[1])
        index <- length(dataStore)+1
        dataStore[[index]] <<- list(
            name=basename(dataFiles[1]),
            mzID=res,
            mzML=raw
            )
        dataFiles <<- dataFiles[-1]
        dataAdded$counter <<- isolate(dataAdded$counter)+1
        
        if(length(dataFiles)) {
            invalidateLater(1, session)
        }

})
    data <- reactive({
        index <- dataAdded$counter
        if(index != 0) {
            do.call('renderData', dataStore[[length(dataStore)]])
        }
    })
    output$result <- reactive({data()})

}
